120	The README says compacted foreground `bash` and `bash_output` notices store raw output under:
121	
122	```text
123	/tmp/tokenjuice/pi-bash-output/
124	```
125	
126	and include a `Read` recovery hint.
127	
128	That is not enough.
129	
130	Required rule:
131	
132	> **If raw output cannot be recovered, tokenjuice must not compact it.**
133	
134	This should apply to all compacted result types, not only foreground bash:
135	
136	* `exec_command`
137	* `bash`
138	* `bash_output`
139	* native Pi `grep`
140	* native Pi `find`
141	* native Pi `ls`
142	* large `Agent` worker results
143	
144	The compacted tool result should include, at minimum:
145	
146	```ts
147	details.tokenjuice = {
148	  compacted: true,
149	  rawPath: "...",
150	  originalBytes: ...,
151	  compactedBytes: ...,
152	  suggestedTools: ["Read", "Grep"],
153	  recoveryHint: "..."
154	}
155	```
156	
157	I would also move raw storage out of unmanaged `/tmp` if this is meant to support serious debugging. Prefer a session-scoped Pi directory, for example:
158	
159	```text
160	~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice/<session-id>/
161	```
162	
163	or under `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.
164	
165	`/tmp` is acceptable for disposable progress logs. It is not acceptable as the only recovery path for CI logs, grep evidence, or worker-agent outputs.
166	
167	### 3. Add conservative thresholds
168	
169	The current README says large Pi `agent` results are compacted at `>=6k visible chars`. That is too low for main-profile use.
170	
171	A safer first-pass policy:
172	
173	| Result type                          |               Initial compaction threshold |
174	| ------------------------------------ | -----------------------------------------: |
175	| `bash_output` repeated progress logs |                       `>=8k visible chars` |
176	| `ls`, `find`                         |                      `>=20k visible chars` |
177	| `grep` / `rg` style results          |                      `>=32k visible chars` |
178	| `exec_command` general output        |                      `>=32k visible chars` |
179	| `Agent` worker output                | `>=50k visible chars`, or exempt initially |
180	
181	Also keep structure:
182	
183	* preserve the command
184	* preserve exit code
185	* preserve first N lines
186	* preserve last N lines
187	* preserve all detected error lines
188	* preserve file paths and line numbers from grep-like output
189	* preserve test summary lines
190	* preserve failure summary lines
191	
192	The point is to compact noise, not destroy the investigative index.
193	
194	### 4. Add an exemption list before activation
195	
196	At minimum, exempt these from lossy or aggressive compaction:
197	
198	#### Tool-level exemptions
199	
200	Keep full:
201	
202	* `web_fetch`
203	* `web_search`
204	* `Read`
205	* planning/read-only agents:
206	
207	  * `explore`
208	  * `plan`
209	  * `decompose`
210	  * `reviewer`
211	
212	The README already claims some of these stay full. I would make that contractual in tests.
213	
214	#### Command-pattern exemptions
215	
216	Do not compact, or only compact with full raw recovery and generous tail retention, for commands matching:
217	
218	```regex
219	\b(vitest|jest|mocha|pytest|cargo test|go test|pnpm test|npm test|yarn test)\b
220	\b(tsc|eslint|biome|ruff|mypy|clippy)\b
221	\b(git diff|git show|git status|git log)\b
222	\b(docker compose logs|kubectl logs|journalctl)\b
223	\b(CI|build|deploy|migration|db:migrate)\b
224	```
225	
226	For these, the middle is often the evidence. A failing test log is not “low signal” just because it is long.
227	
228	For `grep`/`rg`, I would not exempt all of it, but I would require a smarter compactor: preserve every filename, line number, and match summary, then compact repeated match bodies if needed.
229	
230	## Minimal implementation steps
231	
232	I would land this as small diffs:
233	
234	### Diff 1 — metadata and config
235	
236	* Fix tokenjuice peer range for Pi 0.79.0.
237	* Add config defaults, disabled for default profile:
238	
239	```ts
240	PI_TOKENJUICE_ENABLED=0
241	PI_TOKENJUICE_MIN_VISIBLE_CHARS=32000
242	PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=1
243	PI_TOKENJUICE_RAW_DIR=~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice
244	```
245	
246	Do **not** make config affect tool registration. It may affect behavior after tool results, but `tools[]` must remain stable.
247	
248	### Diff 2 — recovery guarantee
249	
250	* Store raw output for every compacted result.
251	* Include `details.tokenjuice.rawPath`.
252	* Add tests that compacted `exec_command`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `bash_output`, and `Agent` results are recoverable.
253	* Add a test that no compaction happens when raw storage fails and `PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=1`.
254	
255	### Diff 3 — exemption and threshold tests
256	
257	Extend `tool-result-hook.test.mjs` to cover:
258	
259	* no compaction below threshold
260	* no compaction for `web_fetch`
261	* no compaction for `explore`, `plan`, `decompose`, `reviewer`
262	* no compaction for test/CI/compiler command patterns
263	* no double-compaction when a TokenJuice notice already exists
264	* raw recovery path exists and contains the original output
265	
266	### Diff 4 — cache-stability smoke
267	
268	Add a request-capture test or harness smoke that proves:
269	
270	```text
271	params.system byte-identical across same-cwd sessions
272	tools[] byte-identical across same-cwd sessions
273	```
274	
275	Run it with:
276	
277	* tokenjuice disabled
278	* tokenjuice enabled
279	* compacted output present
280	* non-compacted output present
281	
282	The key thing: compaction may alter appended tool-result messages. It must not alter the cached system prefix or the tool schema array.
283	
284	## Where I would place it initially
285	
286	Not in `my-pi-full` default.
287	
288	Use one of these instead:
289	
290	```text
291	packages/my-pi-full-tokenjuice-canary
292	```
293	
294	or a static profile variant:
295	
296	```text
297	packages/my-pi-full/package.json
298	packages/my-pi-full-tokenjuice/package.json
299	```

14	 *      that runs in `execute`. `normalizeTaskDraft` is the tolerant-coercion
15	 *      boundary (unwrap legacy `{task}` wrappers, JSON.parse stringified args,
16	 *      map title→subject / body→description); after coercion the result is

19	 *      inside.

## codedb
codedb is a code-intelligence and context tool — not your editor. Use it to understand the codebase before you change it: search, symbol/caller lookup, dependency graph, outlines, and codedb_context for task-shaped orientation. Make edits with your own native file tools. codedb_edit is only a fallback for clients with no native editing.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

80	**hold from default profile → fix gates → run as opt-in canary → promote only if recovery + cache + debugging metrics are clean.**
81	
82	Your current numbers matter here. Pi is already at **90.6% cache hit rate vs Claude Code 93.4%**, with similar parallelism, reads, and tool-per-turn behavior. That means tokenjuice is not solving an urgent parity problem. It is buying possible context savings at the cost of evidence loss, and evidence loss has already cost you real debugging time.
83	
84	The main issue is not whether compaction works. It probably does. The issue is whether it is **lossless enough for investigations**.
85	
86	## Required preconditions before adding it anywhere near the main profile
87	
88	### 1. Fix the peer range and test against the live core
89	
90	`extensions/tokenjuice/package.json` currently says:
91	
92	```json
93	"@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
94	```
95	
96	Your live core is **0.79.0**, so the package metadata says the extension is outside its supported range.
97	
98	Minimum change:
99	
100	```json
101	"@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.79.0 <0.80.0"
102	```
103	
104	or, if you are deliberately supporting both:
105	
106	```json
107	"@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.80.0"
108	```
109	
110	Only do the broader range if the hook API is actually compatible across both.
111	
112	Also note: `packages/my-pi-full/package.json` has the same `<0.79.0` peer range problem for several Pi packages. That is not specific to tokenjuice, but it weakens the profile’s compatibility signal. I would clean that in a separate “0.79 peer range hygiene” changeset.
113	
114	### 2. Make compaction recoverable for every compacted result class
115	
116	Right now there is a mismatch in the facts:
117	
118	The project brief says tokenjuice appends a note that omitted content is **not retrievable**.
119	
120	The README says compacted foreground `bash` and `bash_output` notices store raw output under:
121	
122	```text
123	/tmp/tokenjuice/pi-bash-output/
124	```
125	
126	and include a `Read` recovery hint.
127	
128	That is not enough.
129	
130	Required rule:
131	
132	> **If raw output cannot be recovered, tokenjuice must not compact it.**
133	
134	This should apply to all compacted result types, not only foreground bash:
135	
136	* `exec_command`
137	* `bash`
138	* `bash_output`
139	* native Pi `grep`
140	* native Pi `find`
141	* native Pi `ls`
142	* large `Agent` worker results
143	
144	The compacted tool result should include, at minimum:
145	
146	```ts
147	details.tokenjuice = {
148	  compacted: true,
149	  rawPath: "...",
150	  originalBytes: ...,
151	  compactedBytes: ...,
152	  suggestedTools: ["Read", "Grep"],
153	  recoveryHint: "..."
154	}
155	```
156	
157	I would also move raw storage out of unmanaged `/tmp` if this is meant to support serious debugging. Prefer a session-scoped Pi directory, for example:
158	
159	```text
160	~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice/<session-id>/
161	```
162	
163	or under `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.
164	
165	`/tmp` is acceptable for disposable progress logs. It is not acceptable as the only recovery path for CI logs, grep evidence, or worker-agent outputs.
166	
167	### 3. Add conservative thresholds
168	
169	The current README says large Pi `agent` results are compacted at `>=6k visible chars`. That is too low for main-profile use.
170	
171	A safer first-pass policy:
172	
173	| Result type                          |               Initial compaction threshold |
174	| ------------------------------------ | -----------------------------------------: |
175	| `bash_output` repeated progress logs |                       `>=8k visible chars` |
176	| `ls`, `find`                         |                      `>=20k visible chars` |
177	| `grep` / `rg` style results          |                      `>=32k visible chars` |
178	| `exec_command` general output        |                      `>=32k visible chars` |
179	| `Agent` worker output                | `>=50k visible chars`, or exempt initially |
180	
181	Also keep structure:
182	
183	* preserve the command
184	* preserve exit code
185	* preserve first N lines
186	* preserve last N lines
187	* preserve all detected error lines
188	* preserve file paths and line numbers from grep-like output
189	* preserve test summary lines
190	* preserve failure summary lines
191	
192	The point is to compact noise, not destroy the investigative index.
193	
194	### 4. Add an exemption list before activation
195	
196	At minimum, exempt these from lossy or aggressive compaction:
197	
198	#### Tool-level exemptions
199	
200	Keep full:
201	
202	* `web_fetch`
203	* `web_search`
204	* `Read`
205	* planning/read-only agents:
206	
207	  * `explore`
208	  * `plan`
209	  * `decompose`
210	  * `reviewer`
211	
212	The README already claims some of these stay full. I would make that contractual in tests.
213	
214	#### Command-pattern exemptions
215	
216	Do not compact, or only compact with full raw recovery and generous tail retention, for commands matching:
217	
218	```regex
219	\b(vitest|jest|mocha|pytest|cargo test|go test|pnpm test|npm test|yarn test)\b
220	\b(tsc|eslint|biome|ruff|mypy|clippy)\b
221	\b(git diff|git show|git status|git log)\b
222	\b(docker compose logs|kubectl logs|journalctl)\b
223	\b(CI|build|deploy|migration|db:migrate)\b
224	```
225	
226	For these, the middle is often the evidence. A failing test log is not “low signal” just because it is long.
227	
228	For `grep`/`rg`, I would not exempt all of it, but I would require a smarter compactor: preserve every filename, line number, and match summary, then compact repeated match bodies if needed.
229	
230	## Minimal implementation steps
231	
232	I would land this as small diffs:
233	
234	### Diff 1 — metadata and config
235	
236	* Fix tokenjuice peer range for Pi 0.79.0.
237	* Add config defaults, disabled for default profile:
238	
239	```ts
240	PI_TOKENJUICE_ENABLED=0
241	PI_TOKENJUICE_MIN_VISIBLE_CHARS=32000
242	PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=1
243	PI_TOKENJUICE_RAW_DIR=~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice
244	```
245	
246	Do **not** make config affect tool registration. It may affect behavior after tool results, but `tools[]` must remain stable.
247	
248	### Diff 2 — recovery guarantee
249	
250	* Store raw output for every compacted result.
251	* Include `details.tokenjuice.rawPath`.
252	* Add tests that compacted `exec_command`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `bash_output`, and `Agent` results are recoverable.
253	* Add a test that no compaction happens when raw storage fails and `PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=1`.
254	
255	### Diff 3 — exemption and threshold tests
256	
257	Extend `tool-result-hook.test.mjs` to cover:
258	
259	* no compaction below threshold
260	* no compaction for `web_fetch`
261	* no compaction for `explore`, `plan`, `decompose`, `reviewer`
262	* no compaction for test/CI/compiler command patterns
263	* no double-compaction when a TokenJuice notice already exists
264	* raw recovery path exists and contains the original output
265	
266	### Diff 4 — cache-stability smoke
267	
268	Add a request-capture test or harness smoke that proves:
269	
270	```text
271	params.system byte-identical across same-cwd sessions
272	tools[] byte-identical across same-cwd sessions
273	```
274	
275	Run it with:
276	
277	* tokenjuice disabled
278	* tokenjuice enabled
279	* compacted output present
280	* non-compacted output present
281	
282	The key thing: compaction may alter appended tool-result messages. It must not alter the cached system prefix or the tool schema array.
283	
284	## Where I would place it initially
285	
286	Not in `my-pi-full` default.
287	
288	Use one of these instead:
289	
290	```text
291	packages/my-pi-full-tokenjuice-canary
292	```
293	
294	or a static profile variant:
295	
296	```text
297	packages/my-pi-full/package.json
298	packages/my-pi-full-tokenjuice/package.json
299	```
300	
301	I would avoid a profile where tokenjuice is sometimes loaded and sometimes not loaded depending on environment variables. Load state should be boring. Runtime behavior can be gated, but registration should stay stable.
302	
303	## What would change my mind
304	
305	I would promote tokenjuice into the default profile if a canary showed all of this:
306	
307	1. **At least 15–20% real context reduction** across representative coding sessions, not synthetic logs only.
308	2. **Zero unrecoverable compactions** across debugging sessions.
309	3. **No increase in re-derivation events**, meaning you do not have to rerun commands just because tokenjuice hid useful middle evidence.
310	4. **Byte-stable `params.system` and `tools[]`** across same-cwd sessions.
311	5. **Pi 0.79.0 compatibility tests pass**, with the peer range updated.
312	6. **No regression in session success metrics**, especially failed investigations, extra tool calls, and time-to-fix.
313	
314	Until then, the risk/reward is not good enough for the main profile.
315	
316	---
317	
318	# Decision 2: dream-memory
319	
320	## Verdict
321	
322	**Keep dream-memory out of the Pi profile. Preserve it only for the current A/B window.**
323	
324	So the answer is closest to option **2**, but with a hard expiration:
325	
326	> Keep it out, preserve it for bounded A/B, then retire it unless it beats or materially complements `pi-memory`.
327	
328	I would not choose option 3 now. Re-adding dream-memory creates a known double-injection hazard and adds another model-facing memory path when `pi-memory` already owns the stable base prompt injection.
329	
330	I also would not immediately choose option 1 unless the A/B process is already complete. The audit recommended a 3-memory-backend A/B deadline, and you currently have:
331	
332	* `pi-memory`
333	* `letta-shadow`
334	* `mem0-shadow`
335	
336	in profile as shadows.
337	
338	That is enough experimentation surface. dream-memory should not become a fourth live injector.
339	
340	## Required implementation steps
341	
342	### 1. Make `pi-memory` the explicit sole owner of profile injection
343	
344	Document this in the profile repo, even if only in a short architecture note:
345	
346	```text
347	pi-memory owns model-facing profile memory injection.
348	dream-memory is not loaded in the Pi profile.
349	letta-shadow and mem0-shadow are non-injecting shadows.
350	```
351	
352	This matters because otherwise the same debate will come back every few weeks.
353	
354	### 2. Add a single-owner guard before any possible re-add
355	
356	Even if dream-memory stays out, I would build the guard before anyone is allowed to re-add it.
357	
358	Extension-level, no core patch.
359	
360	Conceptually:
361	
362	```ts
363	const PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER = Symbol.for("valkyriweb.pi.profile-memory-owner");
364	
365	export function claimProfileMemoryOwner(owner: string): boolean {
366	  const g = globalThis as typeof globalThis & {
367	    [PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER]?: string;
368	  };
369	
370	  if (g[PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER] && g[PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER] !== owner) {
371	    return false;
372	  }
373	
374	  g[PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER] = owner;
375	  return true;
376	}
377	```
378	
379	Then:
380	
381	* `pi-memory` claims `profile-base`
382	* dream-memory must check before injecting
383	* if it cannot claim ownership, it must skip model-facing injection and log a diagnostic
384	* the guard must not inject owner metadata into the prompt
385	
386	This guard should cover more than base prompt injection. It should also cover:
387	
388	* `<persistent-memory>` blocks
389	* `<project_instructions>` profile blocks
390	* active recall messages, if they are model-facing
391	* any profile/project memory tail append
392	
393	Otherwise you prevent double base injection but still get double recall.
394	
395	### 3. Keep dream-memory as offline/consolidation-only unless proven otherwise
396	
397	If dream-memory remains useful, split its role mentally:
398	
399	Allowed:
400	
401	* shutdown consolidation
402	* event log processing
403	* markdown wiki maintenance
404	* offline A/B evaluation
405	* cross-harness export/import
406	
407	Not allowed in the Pi profile for now:
408	
409	* SessionStart injection
410	* base prompt injection
411	* project memory injection
412	* active recall injection
413	* extra memory tools that alter `tools[]`
414	
415	That lets you preserve the asset without polluting the runtime profile.
416	
417	### 4. Put a deadline on the memory A/B
418	
419	Use a concrete decision rule. For example:
420	
421	```text
422	By 2026-06-30, or after 30 representative sessions:
423	- choose primary memory path
424	- keep shadows only if they provide measurable lift
425	- retire dream-memory Pi injection unless it wins a defined metric
426	```
427	
428	Metrics I would use:
429	
430	* cache base churn rate
431	* recall precision
432	* recall usefulness judged by whether it changes the next action
433	* user correction rate
434	* duplicate/stale memory rate
435	* tool-call overhead
436	* prompt bytes added per session
437	* number of times memory caused wrong action
438	* number of times memory prevented rework
439	
440	Do not let “interesting architecture” survive without operational evidence.
441	
442	## When I would re-add dream-memory
443	
444	Only re-add it if all of this is true:
445	
446	1. `pi-memory` is not solving a real requirement that dream-memory solves.
447	2. The single-owner guard exists and is tested.
448	3. dream-memory can run with injection disabled by default.
449	4. Any model-facing output is appended at the dynamic tail, never into the cached base, unless it is byte-stable and globally scoped.
450	5. It does not register variable tools based on backend state.
451	6. It has a changeset and a small diff that is easy to revert.
452	
453	The strongest valid reason to re-add it would be: **cross-harness memory consolidation is producing durable, useful memories that `pi-memory` and the shadows do not capture.**
454	
455	The weakest reason would be: **it already exists and used to work.**
456	
457	That is not enough.
458	
459	## What would change my mind
460	
461	I would move from “preserve for A/B” to “retire permanently” if:
462	
463	* `pi-memory` continues to show near-zero churn
464	* `letta-shadow` and `mem0-shadow` provide enough comparison data
465	* dream-memory does not produce measurably better recall
466	* no cross-harness workflow depends on it
467	* it continues to duplicate `pi-memory` responsibilities
468	
469	I would move from “keep out” to “re-add with guard” if:
470	
471	* shutdown consolidation produces materially better long-term memory than `pi-memory`
472	* it reduces repeated context-setting across Pi/Claude Code/Codex
473	* A/B shows better recall precision without prompt bloat
474	* it can run as a non-injecting consolidation backend
475	* a guard proves only one extension can own model-facing memory
476	
477	---
478	
479	# Additional cache-stability risks not named
480	
481	## 1. The profile peer ranges already disagree with the live core
482	
483	This is broader than tokenjuice.
484	
485	`my-pi-full` still declares:
486	
487	```json
488	">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
489	```
490	
491	for several Pi packages while you say the live core is **0.79.0**.
492	
493	Even if runtime works, the metadata is now stale. That can mask real incompatibilities and make future extension audits noisy.
494	
495	I would fix this separately before judging new extension compatibility.
496	
497	## 2. `pi-memory` writes the snapshot non-atomically
498	
499	`renderProfileSnapshot()` uses:
500	
501	```ts
502	await writeFile(path, content ? `${content}\n` : "", "utf8");
503	```
504	
505	A session could theoretically read while the file is being written and inject a partial snapshot.
506	
507	Low probability, but the fix is simple:
508	
509	```text
510	write temp file → fsync if needed → rename atomically
511	```
512	
513	Also avoid rewriting when content hash is unchanged. The cache cares about bytes, not mtime, but unnecessary writes make debugging churn harder.
514	
515	## 3. Snapshot delimiters need broader safety checks
516	
517	`isProfileBaseSafe()` currently rejects:
518	
519	```ts
520	"</project_instructions>"
521	'<project_instructions path="'
522	```
523	
524	I would also reject or escape:
525	
526	```text
527	<project_context>
528	</project_context>
529	SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY
530	<persistent-memory>
531	</persistent-memory>
532	```
533	
534	Any cached-base relocation logic that parses XML-ish prompt blocks can be broken by memory content that accidentally contains control tags.
535	
536	## 4. Absolute paths in prompt tags are stable only if env is stable
537	
538	`blockOpen()` includes:
539	
540	```ts
541	<project_instructions path="${profileSnapshotPath()}">
542	```
543	
544	That path depends on:
545	
546	* `homedir()`
547	* `PI_MEMORY_PROFILE_SNAPSHOT`
548	* runtime user
549	* machine path conventions
550	
551	For same-machine, same-cwd sessions, this is fine. Across machines or changed env, it creates a different cached base. That may be acceptable, but it should be intentional.
552	
553	## 5. dream-memory project memory is more dangerous than profile memory
554	
555	The dream-memory README says its SessionStart equivalent reads:
556	
557	* stable profile memory
558	* auto-detected `memory/project/<cwd-slug>/MEMORY.md`
559	
560	Profile memory can plausibly live in the cross-cwd cached base.
561	
562	Project memory should not.
563	
564	Project memory is cwd-specific and likely to churn more often. If dream-memory ever returns, project memory must live in the dynamic tail or a cwd-specific block that does not contaminate the cross-cwd base.
565	
566	## 6. Shadow backends must stay true shadows
567	
568	`letta-shadow` and `mem0-shadow` are in-profile today. That is fine only if they do not:
569	
570	* inject model-facing memory
571	* register variable tools
572	* change tool descriptions based on backend state
573	* append dynamic context before the cache boundary
574	* fail open into prompt content when an API is reachable
575	
576	“Shadow” should mean observe, write, compare, and report — not influence the model call.
577	
578	## 7. tokenjuice generated-bundle drift is a release risk
579	
580	The README says:
581	
582	```text
583	tokenjuice install pi
584	```
585	
586	can overwrite runtime behavior unless the generated bundle is copied back and verified.
587	
588	That needs a guard.
589	
590	Add one of:
591	
592	* committed generated-bundle hash
593	* smoke test comparing runtime copy to canonical copy
594	* version stamp check in CI
595	* explicit `pnpm verify:tokenjuice-runtime`
596	
597	Otherwise you can review one bundle and run another.
598	
599	---
600	
601	# Final recommendation
602	
603	Do this:
604	
605	1. **Do not add tokenjuice to `my-pi-full` yet.**
606	2. Build a **tokenjuice canary profile** after peer-range, recovery, threshold, exemption, and cache-stability tests are in place.
607	3. **Keep dream-memory out of the Pi profile.**
608	4. Preserve dream-memory only until the memory A/B deadline.
609	5. Add a **single-owner memory injection guard** before any future re-add.
610	6. Clean the Pi 0.79.0 peer ranges across the profile packages.
611	
612	The principle is simple: **do not spend cache stability and debugging evidence to solve a context problem you have not yet proven is hurting you.**

```

Only do the broader range if the hook API is actually compatible across both.

Also note: `packages/my-pi-full/package.json` has the same `<0.79.0` peer range problem for several Pi packages. That is not specific to tokenjuice, but it weakens the profile’s compatibility signal. I would clean that in a separate “0.79 peer range hygiene” changeset.

### 2. Make compaction recoverable for every compacted result class

Right now there is a mismatch in the facts:

The project brief says tokenjuice appends a note that omitted content is **not retrievable**.

The README says compacted foreground `bash` and `bash_output` notices store raw output under:

```text
/tmp/tokenjuice/pi-bash-output/
```

and include a `Read` recovery hint.

That is not enough.

Required rule:

> **If raw output cannot be recovered, tokenjuice must not compact it.**

This should apply to all compacted result types, not only foreground bash:

* `exec_command`
* `bash`
* `bash_output`
* native Pi `grep`
* native Pi `find`
* native Pi `ls`
* large `Agent` worker results

The compacted tool result should include, at minimum:

```ts
details.tokenjuice = {
  compacted: true,
  rawPath: "...",
  originalBytes: ...,
  compactedBytes: ...,
  suggestedTools: ["Read", "Grep"],
  recoveryHint: "..."
}
```

I would also move raw storage out of unmanaged `/tmp` if this is meant to support serious debugging. Prefer a session-scoped Pi directory, for example:

```text
~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice/<session-id>/
```

or under `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.

`/tmp` is acceptable for disposable progress logs. It is not acceptable as the only recovery path for CI logs, grep evidence, or worker-agent outputs.

### 3. Add conservative thresholds

The current README says large Pi `agent` results are compacted at `>=6k visible chars`. That is too low for main-profile use.

A safer first-pass policy:

| Result type                          |               Initial compaction threshold |
| ------------------------------------ | -----------------------------------------: |
| `bash_output` repeated progress logs |                       `>=8k visible chars` |
| `ls`, `find`                         |                      `>=20k visible chars` |
| `grep` / `rg` style results          |                      `>=32k visible chars` |
| `exec_command` general output        |                      `>=32k visible chars` |
| `Agent` worker output                | `>=50k visible chars`, or exempt initially |

Also keep structure:

* preserve the command
* preserve exit code
* preserve first N lines
* preserve last N lines
* preserve all detected error lines
* preserve file paths and line numbers from grep-like output
* preserve test summary lines
* preserve failure summary lines

The point is to compact noise, not destroy the investigative index.

### 4. Add an exemption list before activation

At minimum, exempt these from lossy or aggressive compaction:

#### Tool-level exemptions

Keep full:

* `web_fetch`
* `web_search`
* `Read`
* planning/read-only agents:

  * `explore`
  * `plan`
  * `decompose`
  * `reviewer`

The README already claims some of these stay full. I would make that contractual in tests.

#### Command-pattern exemptions

Do not compact, or only compact with full raw recovery and generous tail retention, for commands matching:

```regex
\b(vitest|jest|mocha|pytest|cargo test|go test|pnpm test|npm test|yarn test)\b
\b(tsc|eslint|biome|ruff|mypy|clippy)\b
\b(git diff|git show|git status|git log)\b
\b(docker compose logs|kubectl logs|journalctl)\b
\b(CI|build|deploy|migration|db:migrate)\b
```

For these, the middle is often the evidence. A failing test log is not “low signal” just because it is long.

For `grep`/`rg`, I would not exempt all of it, but I would require a smarter compactor: preserve every filename, line number, and match summary, then compact repeated match bodies if needed.

## Minimal implementation steps

I would land this as small diffs:

### Diff 1 — metadata and config

* Fix tokenjuice peer range for Pi 0.79.0.
* Add config defaults, disabled for default profile:

```ts
PI_TOKENJUICE_ENABLED=0
PI_TOKENJUICE_MIN_VISIBLE_CHARS=32000
PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=1
PI_TOKENJUICE_RAW_DIR=~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice
```

Do **not** make config affect tool registration. It may affect behavior after tool results, but `tools[]` must remain stable.

### Diff 2 — recovery guarantee

* Store raw output for every compacted result.
* Include `details.tokenjuice.rawPath`.
* Add tests that compacted `exec_command`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `bash_output`, and `Agent` results are recoverable.
* Add a test that no compaction happens when raw storage fails and `PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=1`.

### Diff 3 — exemption and threshold tests

Extend `tool-result-hook.test.mjs` to cover:

* no compaction below threshold
* no compaction for `web_fetch`
* no compaction for `explore`, `plan`, `decompose`, `reviewer`
* no compaction for test/CI/compiler command patterns
* no double-compaction when a TokenJuice notice already exists
* raw recovery path exists and contains the original output

### Diff 4 — cache-stability smoke

Add a request-capture test or harness smoke that proves:

```text
params.system byte-identical across same-cwd sessions
tools[] byte-identical across same-cwd sessions
```

Run it with:

* tokenjuice disabled
* tokenjuice enabled
* compacted output present
* non-compacted output present

The key thing: compaction may alter appended tool-result messages. It must not alter the cached system prefix or the tool schema array.

## Where I would place it initially

Not in `my-pi-full` default.

Use one of these instead:

```text
packages/my-pi-full-tokenjuice-canary
```

or a static profile variant:

```text
packages/my-pi-full/package.json
packages/my-pi-full-tokenjuice/package.json
```

I would avoid a profile where tokenjuice is sometimes loaded and sometimes not loaded depending on environment variables. Load state should be boring. Runtime behavior can be gated, but registration should stay stable.

## What would change my mind

I would promote tokenjuice into the default profile if a canary showed all of this:

1. **At least 15–20% real context reduction** across representative coding sessions, not synthetic logs only.
2. **Zero unrecoverable compactions** across debugging sessions.
3. **No increase in re-derivation events**, meaning you do not have to rerun commands just because tokenjuice hid useful middle evidence.
4. **Byte-stable `params.system` and `tools[]`** across same-cwd sessions.
5. **Pi 0.79.0 compatibility tests pass**, with the peer range updated.
6. **No regression in session success metrics**, especially failed investigations, extra tool calls, and time-to-fix.

Until then, the risk/reward is not good enough for the main profile.

---

# Decision 2: dream-memory

## Verdict

**Keep dream-memory out of the Pi profile. Preserve it only for the current A/B window.**

So the answer is closest to option **2**, but with a hard expiration:

> Keep it out, preserve it for bounded A/B, then retire it unless it beats or materially complements `pi-memory`.

I would not choose option 3 now. Re-adding dream-memory creates a known double-injection hazard and adds another model-facing memory path when `pi-memory` already owns the stable base prompt injection.

I also would not immediately choose option 1 unless the A/B process is already complete. The audit recommended a 3-memory-backend A/B deadline, and you currently have:

* `pi-memory`
* `letta-shadow`
* `mem0-shadow`

in profile as shadows.

That is enough experimentation surface. dream-memory should not become a fourth live injector.

## Required implementation steps

### 1. Make `pi-memory` the explicit sole owner of profile injection

Document this in the profile repo, even if only in a short architecture note:

```text
pi-memory owns model-facing profile memory injection.
dream-memory is not loaded in the Pi profile.
letta-shadow and mem0-shadow are non-injecting shadows.
```

This matters because otherwise the same debate will come back every few weeks.

### 2. Add a single-owner guard before any possible re-add

Even if dream-memory stays out, I would build the guard before anyone is allowed to re-add it.

Extension-level, no core patch.

Conceptually:

```ts
const PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER = Symbol.for("valkyriweb.pi.profile-memory-owner");

export function claimProfileMemoryOwner(owner: string): boolean {
  const g = globalThis as typeof globalThis & {
    [PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER]?: string;
  };

  if (g[PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER] && g[PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER] !== owner) {
    return false;
  }

  g[PROFILE_MEMORY_OWNER] = owner;
  return true;
}
```

Then:

* `pi-memory` claims `profile-base`
* dream-memory must check before injecting
* if it cannot claim ownership, it must skip model-facing injection and log a diagnostic
* the guard must not inject owner metadata into the prompt

This guard should cover more than base prompt injection. It should also cover:

* `<persistent-memory>` blocks
* `<project_instructions>` profile blocks
* active recall messages, if they are model-facing
* any profile/project memory tail append

Otherwise you prevent double base injection but still get double recall.

### 3. Keep dream-memory as offline/consolidation-only unless proven otherwise

If dream-memory remains useful, split its role mentally:

Allowed:

* shutdown consolidation
* event log processing
* markdown wiki maintenance
* offline A/B evaluation
* cross-harness export/import

Not allowed in the Pi profile for now:

* SessionStart injection
* base prompt injection
* project memory injection
* active recall injection
* extra memory tools that alter `tools[]`

That lets you preserve the asset without polluting the runtime profile.

### 4. Put a deadline on the memory A/B

Use a concrete decision rule. For example:

```text
By 2026-06-30, or after 30 representative sessions:
- choose primary memory path
- keep shadows only if they provide measurable lift
- retire dream-memory Pi injection unless it wins a defined metric
```

Metrics I would use:

* cache base churn rate
* recall precision
* recall usefulness judged by whether it changes the next action
* user correction rate
* duplicate/stale memory rate
* tool-call overhead
* prompt bytes added per session
* number of times memory caused wrong action
* number of times memory prevented rework

Do not let “interesting architecture” survive without operational evidence.

## When I would re-add dream-memory

Only re-add it if all of this is true:

1. `pi-memory` is not solving a real requirement that dream-memory solves.
2. The single-owner guard exists and is tested.
3. dream-memory can run with injection disabled by default.
4. Any model-facing output is appended at the dynamic tail, never into the cached base, unless it is byte-stable and globally scoped.
5. It does not register variable tools based on backend state.
6. It has a changeset and a small diff that is easy to revert.

The strongest valid reason to re-add it would be: **cross-harness memory consolidation is producing durable, useful memories that `pi-memory` and the shadows do not capture.**

The weakest reason would be: **it already exists and used to work.**

That is not enough.

## What would change my mind

I would move from “preserve for A/B” to “retire permanently” if:

* `pi-memory` continues to show near-zero churn
* `letta-shadow` and `mem0-shadow` provide enough comparison data
* dream-memory does not produce measurably better recall
* no cross-harness workflow depends on it
* it continues to duplicate `pi-memory` responsibilities

I would move from “keep out” to “re-add with guard” if:

* shutdown consolidation produces materially better long-term memory than `pi-memory`
* it reduces repeated context-setting across Pi/Claude Code/Codex
* A/B shows better recall precision without prompt bloat
* it can run as a non-injecting consolidation backend
* a guard proves only one extension can own model-facing memory

---

# Additional cache-stability risks not named

## 1. The profile peer ranges already disagree with the live core

This is broader than tokenjuice.

`my-pi-full` still declares:

```json
">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
```

for several Pi packages while you say the live core is **0.79.0**.

Even if runtime works, the metadata is now stale. That can mask real incompatibilities and make future extension audits noisy.

I would fix this separately before judging new extension compatibility.

## 2. `pi-memory` writes the snapshot non-atomically

`renderProfileSnapshot()` uses:

```ts
await writeFile(path, content ? `${content}\n` : "", "utf8");
```

A session could theoretically read while the file is being written and inject a partial snapshot.

Low probability, but the fix is simple:

```text
write temp file → fsync if needed → rename atomically
```

Also avoid rewriting when content hash is unchanged. The cache cares about bytes, not mtime, but unnecessary writes make debugging churn harder.

## 3. Snapshot delimiters need broader safety checks

`isProfileBaseSafe()` currently rejects:

```ts
"</project_instructions>"
'<project_instructions path="'
```

I would also reject or escape:

```text
<project_context>
</project_context>
SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY
<persistent-memory>
</persistent-memory>
```

Any cached-base relocation logic that parses XML-ish prompt blocks can be broken by memory content that accidentally contains control tags.

## 4. Absolute paths in prompt tags are stable only if env is stable

`blockOpen()` includes:

```ts
<project_instructions path="${profileSnapshotPath()}">
```

That path depends on:

* `homedir()`
* `PI_MEMORY_PROFILE_SNAPSHOT`
* runtime user
* machine path conventions

For same-machine, same-cwd sessions, this is fine. Across machines or changed env, it creates a different cached base. That may be acceptable, but it should be intentional.

## 5. dream-memory project memory is more dangerous than profile memory

The dream-memory README says its SessionStart equivalent reads:

* stable profile memory
* auto-detected `memory/project/<cwd-slug>/MEMORY.md`

Profile memory can plausibly live in the cross-cwd cached base.

Project memory should not.

Project memory is cwd-specific and likely to churn more often. If dream-memory ever returns, project memory must live in the dynamic tail or a cwd-specific block that does not contaminate the cross-cwd base.

## 6. Shadow backends must stay true shadows

`letta-shadow` and `mem0-shadow` are in-profile today. That is fine only if they do not:

* inject model-facing memory
* register variable tools
* change tool descriptions based on backend state
* append dynamic context before the cache boundary
* fail open into prompt content when an API is reachable

“Shadow” should mean observe, write, compare, and report — not influence the model call.

## 7. tokenjuice generated-bundle drift is a release risk

The README says:

```text
tokenjuice install pi
```

can overwrite runtime behavior unless the generated bundle is copied back and verified.

That needs a guard.

Add one of:

* committed generated-bundle hash
* smoke test comparing runtime copy to canonical copy
* version stamp check in CI
* explicit `pnpm verify:tokenjuice-runtime`

Otherwise you can review one bundle and run another.

---

# Final recommendation

Do this:

1. **Do not add tokenjuice to `my-pi-full` yet.**
2. Build a **tokenjuice canary profile** after peer-range, recovery, threshold, exemption, and cache-stability tests are in place.
3. **Keep dream-memory out of the Pi profile.**
4. Preserve dream-memory only until the memory A/B deadline.
5. Add a **single-owner memory injection guard** before any future re-add.
6. Clean the Pi 0.79.0 peer ranges across the profile packages.

The principle is simple: **do not spend cache stability and debugging evidence to solve a context problem you have not yet proven is hurting you.**

Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. Fork-hygiene ADR: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`. Active program: `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-2026-05-30T07-50-47Z-pi-platform-program.md`.

## Key repos & paths

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Pi fork (core binary) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent`) |
| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` at `http://127.0.0.1:9100` |
| Extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |
| Bridge / cache-health / routine launch agents | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi.claude-bridge.plist`, `com.luke.pi-cache-health.plist`, `com.pi-routine.*.plist` |
| Model metadata (bridge provider) | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (Opus 4.8 = `claude-opus-4-8`, `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`) |
| Extension API reference / best practices | `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md`, `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` |
| Setup registry (catalog YAML = source; `generated/` scanner-owned, never hand-edit) | `my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` |
| Runtime fleet map ("where does this pi call go?") | `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| Release engineering (versioned registry, CI gates, rollback, binary dist) | `my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` |
| Config layering (L1–L4 model, `extensionConfig` contract) | `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` |

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**:

1. Make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials.
2. Coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases.

Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Config layering

Deep detail: `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md`.

| Layer | Name | Mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Capability | extension source defaults | `const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 5` |
| L2 | Membership | profile manifest `pi.extensions[]` | including/excluding an extension |
| L3 | Tuning | `settings.json` `extensionConfig{}`, deep-merged global ← project | `extensionConfig["cache-base-prompt"].extendBase = true` |
| L4 | Override | env var / CLI `--flag` via `registerFlag`/`getFlag` | `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1` |

- Keep defaults in extension-owned config files or typed source defaults; keep operator tuning in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json`; use env vars only as L4 overrides for one-off runs, secrets, CI, or emergency flips.
- New extension settings go in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json` — never new top-level `Settings` keys, never env-only configuration.
- `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor on `ExtensionAPI` is the missing ~15 LOC piece (`createExtensionAPI` has no settings handle yet — `loader.ts:254`); track as `fork-first (platform)` until upstreamed. Until it lands, extensions may read `settings.json` directly, then apply env overrides.

## Cache & system-prompt stability

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- **Cross-cwd base-extend lever: `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`** (set in `~/.zshenv` — zsh never sources `~/.profile`, so a copy there is dead). `cache-base-prompt` ext relocates the dynamic boundary so the global AGENTS chain + `<available_skills>` ride **block0** (cross-cwd shared base, cached once) instead of per-cwd **block1** (re-cached per project) — moves ~14K tok cross-cwd, `tools[]` unchanged, content-preserving. Gate: `node extensions/cache-base-prompt/test.mjs`. This is the lever for project/directory-specific caching.
- **`setActiveTools` is NOT idempotent** (fork `agent-harness.ts:941` always emits `tools_update` + a session write, even for an unchanged set — the documented "builtins removed ~2,560×/18d" burst source). An extension calling it per-turn from `before_agent_start` must guard: `if (sameNames(pi.getActiveTools(), desired)) return;` before the call, or it bursts the within-session `tools[]` cache. Pattern: `tool-search`; `advisor` now guarded too.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.
- Verification gate after any extension/harness/skill change: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate` + `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.
- Deferred-tool contracts (situational/heavy extension tools must set `deferLoading: true`): `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:deferred-tool-contracts`. Prefer `tool_reference` / provider-native `defer_loading` over mutating active tools after `tool_search`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What This Is

A memory extension for the [pi coding agent](https://github.com/mariozechner/pi-mono). It provides persistent memory across coding sessions via plain markdown files, with optional semantic search powered by [qmd](https://github.com/tobi/qmd). Single-file extension (`index.ts`) — no build step, pi loads TypeScript directly.

## Commands

```bash
# Run e2e tests (requires `pi` on PATH with a configured API key)
bun test/e2e.ts

# Test the extension manually with pi
pi -p -e ./index.ts "remember: I prefer dark mode"

# Install into pi
pi install ./pi-memory
```

## Architecture

The entire extension is `index.ts` — a single default export function that receives pi's `ExtensionAPI` and:

1. **Registers lifecycle hooks**: `session_start` (detect qmd), `session_shutdown` (cleanup), `before_agent_start` (inject memory context into system prompt every turn), `session_before_compact` (warn about compaction)
2. **Registers 4 tools**: `memory_write`, `memory_read`, `scratchpad`, `memory_search`
3. **Manages files under `~/.pi/agent/memory/`**: `MEMORY.md` (long-term), `SCRATCHPAD.md` (checklist), `daily/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` (append-only logs)

Key design patterns:
- Context injection via `before_agent_start` loads MEMORY.md + open scratchpad items + today/yesterday daily logs into the system prompt before every agent turn
- qmd integration is optional and detected at runtime — core tools work without it, only `memory_search` requires qmd
- After every write, a debounced (500ms) `qmd update` runs fire-and-forget in the background
- Scratchpad items are stored as markdown checklists with HTML comment metadata (`<!-- timestamp [sessionId] -->`)

## Peer Dependencies

Uses `@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent` (ExtensionAPI types, Luke's `pi-mono-fork`), `@valkyriweb/pi-ai` (StringEnum), and `@sinclair/typebox` (schema definitions). These are peer deps — provided by the pi runtime. Upstream is `@mariozechner/*`; the fork republishes under `@earendil-works/*`.

## Testing

Tests are e2e only — they invoke `pi` as a subprocess with the extension loaded, send LLM prompts, and verify tool calls happened and files were written. Tests back up and restore `~/.pi/agent/memory/` files automatically. Each test runs a fresh `pi --no-session` invocation.

# Tokenjuice Pi extension

Canonical copy of the generated Tokenjuice Pi extension used by Luke's Pi runtime.

The generated bundle comes from:

```bash
tokenjuice install pi
```

Current bundled version is stamped in `tokenjuice.generated.js`.

Runtime install is a real file at:

```text
~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js
```

That runtime file is a copied generated bundle; it is intentionally not a
symlink.

Important: this generated bundle has local support for:

- Codex-adapter `exec_command` / `write_stdin` result shapes.
- Native Pi `grep` / `find` / `ls` result shapes, mapped to TokenJuice `exec` rules with `pi-native-*` metadata.
- Large Pi `agent` results only (>=6k visible chars), mapped with `pi-agent` metadata and a higher savings threshold to avoid compacting normal summaries.
- Model-aware child-agent compaction: Sonnet/Opus and GPT-5.4-mini/GPT-5.5 child tools compact, while Haiku and GPT-5.3 Codex Spark/Sparks stay full.
- Direct WebFetch/WebSearch results and read-only/planning agent outputs (`explore`, `plan`, `decompose`, `reviewer`) stay full.
- Pi `bash_output` results, including background jobs that only expose `bgId`, with a tighter inline budget so repeated progress logs do not replay hundreds of lines into the session.
- Compacted foreground `bash` and `bash_output` notices always store the raw output under `/tmp/tokenjuice/pi-bash-output/` and include a `Read` recovery hint pointing at that file.
- `details.tokenjuice` includes `rawPath`, `suggestedTools: ["Read", "Grep"]`, and a recovery hint so agents can inspect raw output without replaying it.
- Outputs that already contain a TokenJuice notice are left untouched to avoid nested/double compaction notices.

Re-running `tokenjuice install pi` can overwrite runtime behavior unless the generated bundle is copied back here and verified.

1	# Memory Architecture
2	
3	Two parallel systems handle persistence across Pi sessions. They serve different roles and complement each other.
4	
5	**Full internals comparison:** [`memory-systems-comparison.md`](./memory-systems-comparison.md) — source-backed deep dive vs Claude Code + Codex.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Systems at a glance
10	
11	| | dream-memory | pi-memory |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **Role** | Read path — inject context at session start; owns 24h/N-session consolidation (CC `autoDream`) | Write path — per-turn memory extraction (CC `extractMemories`) |
14	| **Storage root** | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
15	| **Trigger** | `dispatchSessionStart` (once per session, turn 1) | `turn_end` hook, per-turn (throttle `PI_MEMORY_MIN_NEW_TURNS`, default 1); no time/session gate |
16	| **Injection point** | Stable `<persistent-memory>` snapshot (turn 1 only; cache-safe) | Per-turn fork (`maxTurns: 5`) + shutdown flush; active recall appends at the message tail when enabled |
17	| **Source extension** | `my-pi/extensions/dream-memory/` | `my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/` |
18	| **Key entrypoint** | `src/harness-cli.ts` | `index.ts` |
19	| **Subagent** | None (file read only) | `general` (forked, bounded toolset) |
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Merge status (2026-06-02)
24	
25	dream→pi-memory consolidation in progress. Current reality:
26	
27	- **dream-memory is `retired`** — in no profile manifest (`my-pi-full` loads only `pi-memory`); `harness-cli.ts` is dead code. Kept for migration reference.
28	- **Profile injection moved into pi-memory** (read-path responsibility): the `pi-memory.profile-base` `systemPrompt:build` filter (priority 10) injects a byte-stable snapshot rendered from the curated obsidian profile files (`00-pi-active-context.md` + `MEMORY.md`) into the cacheable base. `cache-base-prompt` (priority 90, `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`) relocates it cross-cwd. Snapshot file: `~/.pi/agent/dream-memory/profile-memory.md`; refreshed on `session_start` when stale (tracks the hourly autoDream run). See `extensions/pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts`.
29	- **Obsidian-tree consolidation still runs** via the `dream-consolidation` routine (`pnpm dream pending`, watched by `com.pi-routine.watch-dream-consolidation`, gated to ~hourly). Its prompt already mirrors the instruction-refiner + progressive-disclosure discipline (`dream/dream.ts:654`). pi-tree extraction (per-turn) is unchanged.
30	- **Recall UX** (pi-memory): hits deliver as a single collapsible thinking-styled custom message (`pi_memory_recall`) on the next turn, past the cache breakpoint — not a user-text transform; slim footer `🧠 N · Xms`. See `src/recall-message.ts`.
31	- **qmd inline recall is ON (resolved 2026-06-02, qmd 2.5.3).** The 2.5.1 SIGABRT-on-teardown was an upstream darwin-Metal bug: the `ggml_metal_device` destructor asserts `[rsets->data count] == 0` during `__cxa_finalize_ranges`, only firing when `process.exit()` skips Node's `beforeExit` (which node-llama-cpp uses to dispose Metal contexts). Fixed upstream in tobi/qmd 2.5.3 (`finishSuccessfulCliCommand` sets `process.exitCode = 0` and returns instead of calling `process.exit(0)`). No local patch needed — bumped the global binary `@tobilu/qmd` 2.5.1→2.5.3 (`npm i -g @tobilu/qmd@latest`). After the upgrade, `qmd query` exits 0 and federated multi-collection recall returns correct hits (the earlier `vsearch` 0-hits was 2.1-era flakiness; resolved post-embed-repair). Recall path is now the **structured reranked `qmd query`** (`vec:`+`lex:` lines supplied by us → skips the ~20 s LLM HyDE auto-expansion but keeps the reranker; `qmd search` drops rerank, `qmd vsearch` is vector-only), federated via repeated `-c` across `pi-memory` + `dream-memory-{profile,project,tools}`. Warm latency ~1.0–1.3 s (timeout ceiling 3000 ms); a cold MLX embedder/reranker reload after idle can spike to ~16 s for a novel query, so on a cold miss the recall **gracefully falls back to the in-process lexical scan** (no crash, no hang) and steady-state turns get federated reranked qmd hits. The merge respects `route`: when `route:"qmd"` returns hits they ARE the result (qmd's 0–1 rerank scores are otherwise buried under the lexical term-frequency counts); lexical is the fallback only when qmd is empty. Recall still blocks the turn so hits land in-turn (quality over latency, per Luke; `extensions/pi-memory/index.ts` input handler). Config: `recall.route:"qmd"`, `recall.qmd.enabled:true`, `recall.qmd.collections:[…]` in `config/defaults.json` + `src/config.ts`; wiring in `src/qmd.ts:searchQmdCli`. The warm-REST alternative (`searchQmdHttp`) federates the same collections if a `qmd serve` listener is ever enabled (`httpPort`).
32	
33	---
34	
35	## dream-memory — read path
36	
37	Injects a deterministic subset of `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` on the **first turn of every session**. This is a cache-stable snapshot, not a live recall feed.
38	
39	Hard caps: **24 kB total / 8 files**. YAML frontmatter is stripped before injection so event ids, dream timestamps, and other provenance fields do not change the cached prompt prefix.
40	
41	**Loader order** (lex-sorted within each root, stops at cap):
42	
43	1. `profile/` — durable cross-project preferences, identity, tooling config
44	2. `project/<slug>/` — only when cwd resolves to that slug (via `.dream-memory.yml` or git remote)
45	3. repowise summary (`.repowise/` index, if present in repo)
46	
47	**Not injected into the cached prefix** (but indexed; accessible via active recall or dream consolidation):
48	- `inbox/` — raw uncurated notes
49	- `archive/` — session logs, RCAs, one-off notes
50	- `tools/`, `memory-archive-*/`
51	
52	**Anchor file:** `profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — loads first (lex-sort), ≤1500 tok briefing card. Keep it **cache-stable**: no dates, no session counters, no event ids.
53	
54	**Config:** `DREAM_WIKI_HOME=~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`
55	
56	---
57	
58	## pi-memory — write path
59	
60	Consolidates session learning into structured memory files. Uses Claude Code's `memdir/` storage shape (same type taxonomy, filename convention, frontmatter shape, MEMORY.md index pattern), but Pi keeps the main-session prompt compact: the parent sees memory availability, safety, and minimal inline-write guidance; the full write protocol lives in the extractor prompt and `pi-memory-save` skill.
61	
62	**On-disk layout:**
63	
64	```
65	~/.pi/agent/memory/
66	├── profile/
67	│   ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (cross-project memories)
68	│   ├── user_*.md
69	│   └── feedback_*.md
70	└── project/<slug>/
71	    ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (project-specific memories)
72	    ├── project_*.md
73	    └── reference_*.md
74	```
75	
76	**Type taxonomy:** `user | feedback | project | reference`
77	
78	**Trigger gates (v3, 2026-05-16):**
79	
80	| Gate | Default | Env override |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| Time since last consolidation | 24 h | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS` |
83	| Sessions since last consolidation | 5 | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS` |
84	| Re-scan throttle | 10 min | `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS` |
85	| Cross-process lock | per-scope `.consolidate-lock-<scope>` mtime file | — |
86	| Pollution skip | sessions with `web_search`, `mcp_*`, `WebFetch` | `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_OVERRIDES_PRIORITY=1` |
87	
88	**Prompt templates:** `extensions/pi-memory/prompts/`
89	
90	---
91	
92	## Active-recall — the bridge between the two
93	
94	`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory.ts` provides the experimental **per-turn read side** for both stores. It can rank `qmd` vector-index hits across federated collections and inject relevant memories as a custom message. Delivery is cache-safe only when the Pi extension filters stale active-recall messages out of the transcript view and appends the current settled recall at the tail of the next model call.
95	
96	**Collections in default recall:**
97	
98	| Collection | Backs |
99	|---|---|
100	| `pi-memory` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
101	| `dream-memory-profile` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` |
102	| `dream-memory-project` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/` |
103	| `scars` | scar-tissue patterns |
104	| `changes` | notable change log entries |
105	
106	**Enable:** set `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1` for an explicit live opt-in, or edit `~/.dream-memory/recall.toml` to `enabled = true`. `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=0` remains a kill switch.
107	
108	**Circuit breaker:** fires only if `candidate_limit` (40) hits pass a relevance threshold (`auto_none_threshold` 0.4). Never fires inside pi-memory subagents (`isPiMemorySubAgent` guard).
109	
110	---
111	
112	## Adding memories manually
113	
114	| What | Where |
115	|---|---|
116	| Durable cross-project preference | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/<topic>.md` |
117	| Project-specific fact | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/<slug>/<topic>.md` |
118	| Quick inbox note | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/inbox/<name>.md` (vector-indexed only; not injected) |
119	| Session learning (auto) | pi-memory writes to `~/.pi/agent/memory/` after the session |
120	
121	---
122	
123	## Diagnosing bloat
124	
125	```bash
126	pi-cache-stats --all   # watch turn-1 `write` column
127	```
128	
129	A clean baseline from `~/Projects/personal/<repo>` sits at ≤ ~35 kB write on turn 1. If it jumps:
130	
131	1. Audit `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` — keep total ≤ 3 kB
132	2. Check `project/<slug>/` for large files; move bulk content to `archive/`
133	3. Verify `inbox/` is draining through dream; it should be indexed/searchable, not first-turn injected
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Related docs
138	
139	| Doc | When to read |
140	|---|---|
141	| [`memory-systems-comparison.md`](./memory-systems-comparison.md) | Source-backed deep dive; CC + Codex comparison; v3 gap analysis |
142	| [`cache-strategy.md`](./cache-strategy.md) | How memory extraction avoids cache breaks in forked agents |
143	| `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md` | Mandatory checklist when touching fork/extension memory code |

31	- **qmd inline recall is ON (resolved 2026-06-02, qmd 2.5.3).** The 2.5.1 SIGABRT-on-teardown was an upstream darwin-Metal bug: the `ggml_metal_device` destructor asserts `[rsets->data count] == 0` during `__cxa_finalize_ranges`, only firing when `process.exit()` skips Node's `beforeExit` (which node-llama-cpp uses to dispose Metal contexts). Fixed upstream in tobi/qmd 2.5.3 (`finishSuccessfulCliCommand` sets `process.exitCode = 0` and returns instead of calling `process.exit(0)`). No local patch needed — bumped the global binary `@tobilu/qmd` 2.5.1→2.5.3 (`npm i -g @tobilu/qmd@latest`). # Memory Architecture

Two parallel systems handle persistence across Pi sessions. They serve different roles and complement each other.

**Full internals comparison:** [`memory-systems-comparison.md`](./memory-systems-comparison.md) — source-backed deep dive vs Claude Code + Codex.

---

## Systems at a glance

| | dream-memory | pi-memory |
|---|---|---|
| **Role** | Read path — inject context at session start; owns 24h/N-session consolidation (CC `autoDream`) | Write path — per-turn memory extraction (CC `extractMemories`) |
| **Storage root** | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
| **Trigger** | `dispatchSessionStart` (once per session, turn 1) | `turn_end` hook, per-turn (throttle `PI_MEMORY_MIN_NEW_TURNS`, default 1); no time/session gate |
| **Injection point** | Stable `<persistent-memory>` snapshot (turn 1 only; cache-safe) | Per-turn fork (`maxTurns: 5`) + shutdown flush; active recall appends at the message tail when enabled |
| **Source extension** | `my-pi/extensions/dream-memory/` | `my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/` |
| **Key entrypoint** | `src/harness-cli.ts` | `index.ts` |
| **Subagent** | None (file read only) | `general` (forked, bounded toolset) |

---

## Merge status (2026-06-02)

dream→pi-memory consolidation in progress. Current reality:

- **dream-memory is `retired`** — in no profile manifest (`my-pi-full` loads only `pi-memory`); `harness-cli.ts` is dead code. Kept for migration reference.
- **Profile injection moved into pi-memory** (read-path responsibility): the `pi-memory.profile-base` `systemPrompt:build` filter (priority 10) injects a byte-stable snapshot rendered from the curated obsidian profile files (`00-pi-active-context.md` + `MEMORY.md`) into the cacheable base. `cache-base-prompt` (priority 90, `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`) relocates it cross-cwd. Snapshot file: `~/.pi/agent/dream-memory/profile-memory.md`; refreshed on `session_start` when stale (tracks the hourly autoDream run). See `extensions/pi-memory/src/profile-base.ts`.
- **Obsidian-tree consolidation still runs** via the `dream-consolidation` routine (`pnpm dream pending`, watched by `com.pi-routine.watch-dream-consolidation`, gated to ~hourly). Its prompt already mirrors the instruction-refiner + progressive-disclosure discipline (`dream/dream.ts:654`). pi-tree extraction (per-turn) is unchanged.
- **Recall UX** (pi-memory): hits deliver as a single collapsible thinking-styled custom message (`pi_memory_recall`) on the next turn, past the cache breakpoint — not a user-text transform; slim footer `🧠 N · Xms`. See `src/recall-message.ts`.
- **qmd inline recall is ON (resolved 2026-06-02, qmd 2.5.3).** The 2.5.1 SIGABRT-on-teardown was an upstream darwin-Metal bug: the `ggml_metal_device` destructor asserts `[rsets->data count] == 0` during `__cxa_finalize_ranges`, only firing when `process.exit()` skips Node's `beforeExit` (which node-llama-cpp uses to dispose Metal contexts). Fixed upstream in tobi/qmd 2.5.3 (`finishSuccessfulCliCommand` sets `process.exitCode = 0` and returns instead of calling `process.exit(0)`). No local patch needed — bumped the global binary `@tobilu/qmd` 2.5.1→2.5.3 (`npm i -g @tobilu/qmd@latest`). After the upgrade, `qmd query` exits 0 and federated multi-collection recall returns correct hits (the earlier `vsearch` 0-hits was 2.1-era flakiness; resolved post-embed-repair). Recall path is now the **structured reranked `qmd query`** (`vec:`+`lex:` lines supplied by us → skips the ~20 s LLM HyDE auto-expansion but keeps the reranker; `qmd search` drops rerank, `qmd vsearch` is vector-only), federated via repeated `-c` across `pi-memory` + `dream-memory-{profile,project,tools}`. Warm latency ~1.0–1.3 s (timeout ceiling 3000 ms); a cold MLX embedder/reranker reload after idle can spike to ~16 s for a novel query, so on a cold miss the recall **gracefully falls back to the in-process lexical scan** (no crash, no hang) and steady-state turns get federated reranked qmd hits. The merge respects `route`: when `route:"qmd"` returns hits they ARE the result (qmd's 0–1 rerank scores are otherwise buried under the lexical term-frequency counts); lexical is the fallback only when qmd is empty. Recall still blocks the turn so hits land in-turn (quality over latency, per Luke; `extensions/pi-memory/index.ts` input handler). Config: `recall.route:"qmd"`, `recall.qmd.enabled:true`, `recall.qmd.collections:[…]` in `config/defaults.json` + `src/config.ts`; wiring in `src/qmd.ts:searchQmdCli`. The warm-REST alternative (`searchQmdHttp`) federates the same collections if a `qmd serve` listener is ever enabled (`httpPort`).

---

## dream-memory — read path

Injects a deterministic subset of `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/` on the **first turn of every session**. This is a cache-stable snapshot, not a live recall feed.

Hard caps: **24 kB total / 8 files**. YAML frontmatter is stripped before injection so event ids, dream timestamps, and other provenance fields do not change the cached prompt prefix.

**Loader order** (lex-sorted within each root, stops at cap):

1. `profile/` — durable cross-project preferences, identity, tooling config
2. `project/<slug>/` — only when cwd resolves to that slug (via `.dream-memory.yml` or git remote)
3. repowise summary (`.repowise/` index, if present in repo)

**Not injected into the cached prefix** (but indexed; accessible via active recall or dream consolidation):
- `inbox/` — raw uncurated notes
- `archive/` — session logs, RCAs, one-off notes
- `tools/`, `memory-archive-*/`

**Anchor file:** `profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — loads first (lex-sort), ≤1500 tok briefing card. Keep it **cache-stable**: no dates, no session counters, no event ids.

**Config:** `DREAM_WIKI_HOME=~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/`

---

## pi-memory — write path

Consolidates session learning into structured memory files. Uses Claude Code's `memdir/` storage shape (same type taxonomy, filename convention, frontmatter shape, MEMORY.md index pattern), but Pi keeps the main-session prompt compact: the parent sees memory availability, safety, and minimal inline-write guidance; the full write protocol lives in the extractor prompt and `pi-memory-save` skill.

**On-disk layout:**

```
~/.pi/agent/memory/
├── profile/
│   ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (cross-project memories)
│   ├── user_*.md
│   └── feedback_*.md
└── project/<slug>/
    ├── MEMORY.md              ← index (project-specific memories)
    ├── project_*.md
    └── reference_*.md
```

**Type taxonomy:** `user | feedback | project | reference`

**Trigger gates (v3, 2026-05-16):**

| Gate | Default | Env override |
|---|---|---|
| Time since last consolidation | 24 h | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS` |
| Sessions since last consolidation | 5 | `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS` |
| Re-scan throttle | 10 min | `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS` |
| Cross-process lock | per-scope `.consolidate-lock-<scope>` mtime file | — |
| Pollution skip | sessions with `web_search`, `mcp_*`, `WebFetch` | `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_OVERRIDES_PRIORITY=1` |

**Prompt templates:** `extensions/pi-memory/prompts/`

---

## Active-recall — the bridge between the two

`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory.ts` provides the experimental **per-turn read side** for both stores. It can rank `qmd` vector-index hits across federated collections and inject relevant memories as a custom message. Delivery is cache-safe only when the Pi extension filters stale active-recall messages out of the transcript view and appends the current settled recall at the tail of the next model call.

**Collections in default recall:**

| Collection | Backs |
|---|---|
| `pi-memory` | `~/.pi/agent/memory/` |
| `dream-memory-profile` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` |
| `dream-memory-project` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/` |
| `scars` | scar-tissue patterns |
| `changes` | notable change log entries |

**Enable:** set `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1` for an explicit live opt-in, or edit `~/.dream-memory/recall.toml` to `enabled = true`. `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=0` remains a kill switch.

**Circuit breaker:** fires only if `candidate_limit` (40) hits pass a relevance threshold (`auto_none_threshold` 0.4). Never fires inside pi-memory subagents (`isPiMemorySubAgent` guard).

---

## Adding memories manually

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Durable cross-project preference | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/<topic>.md` |
| Project-specific fact | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/project/<slug>/<topic>.md` |
| Quick inbox note | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/inbox/<name>.md` (vector-indexed only; not injected) |
| Session learning (auto) | pi-memory writes to `~/.pi/agent/memory/` after the session |

---

## Diagnosing bloat

```bash
pi-cache-stats --all   # watch turn-1 `write` column
```

A clean baseline from `~/Projects/personal/<repo>` sits at ≤ ~35 kB write on turn 1. If it jumps:

1. Audit `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/` — keep total ≤ 3 kB
2. Check `project/<slug>/` for large files; move bulk content to `archive/`
3. Verify `inbox/` is draining through dream; it should be indexed/searchable, not first-turn injected

---
