- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Tokenjuice Pi extension

Canonical copy of the generated Tokenjuice Pi extension, wrapped in a house
policy layer. **Canary-only** per the oracle verdict 2026-06-09
(`docs/pi-harness-optimisation/2026-06-08/findings/oracle-tokenjuice-dream-memory-verdict.md`):
not in `my-pi-full` — `scripts/check-profiles.mjs` rejects it there — load it
via the `@valkyriweb/my-pi-full-tokenjuice-canary` profile.

## Policy layer (`policy.mjs`)

`index.js` exports the generated bundle wrapped in `withPolicy()`. The bundle
stays pristine (regenerable); every house opinion lives in the wrapper:

| Rule | Default |
|---|---|
| Enabled | yes when loaded (profile membership = opt-in); `PI_TOKENJUICE_ENABLED=0` or `extensionConfig.tokenjuice.enabled=false` kills |
| Visible-char floors | bash/bash_output 8k · ls/find 20k · grep/exec 32k (`PI_TOKENJUICE_MIN_VISIBLE_CHARS` overrides all) |
| Agent results | exempt entirely (`PI_TOKENJUICE_COMPACT_AGENTS=1` re-enables at a 50k floor) |
| Evidence commands | test/CI/compiler/git-diff/log patterns never compact |
| Raw recovery | compaction without a readable raw file is **dropped** (`PI_TOKENJUICE_REQUIRE_RAW_RECOVERY=0` waives) |
| Raw location | relocated from `/tmp` to `~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice/` (`PI_TOKENJUICE_RAW_DIR`) |

Config layering: defaults above (L1) ← `extensionConfig.tokenjuice` in
settings.json (L3) ← `PI_TOKENJUICE_*` env (L4).

Tests: `npm run test:tokenjuice:smoke` (bundle contract + policy contract +
cache-stability smoke). Drift guard: `npm run verify:tokenjuice-runtime`
(runtime install at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` must be
byte-identical to the canonical bundle, or absent).

## Promotion criteria (canary → my-pi-full)

All six, from the verdict: ≥15–20% real context reduction on representative
sessions; zero unrecoverable compactions; no increase in re-derivation events;
byte-stable `params.system`/`tools[]`; peer-range/compat tests green; no
regression in failed investigations, extra tool calls, or time-to-fix.

# Tokenjuice Pi extension

Canonical copy of the generated Tokenjuice Pi extension used by Luke's Pi runtime.

The generated bundle comes from:

```bash
tokenjuice install pi
```

Current bundled version is stamped in `tokenjuice.generated.js`.

Runtime install is a real file at:

```text
~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js
```

That runtime file is a copied generated bundle; it is intentionally not a
symlink.

Important: this generated bundle has local support for:

- Codex-adapter `exec_command` / `write_stdin` result shapes.
- Native Pi `grep` / `find` / `ls` result shapes, mapped to TokenJuice `exec` rules with `pi-native-*` metadata.
- Large Pi `agent` results only (>=6k visible chars), mapped with `pi-agent` metadata and a higher savings threshold to avoid compacting normal summaries.
- Model-aware child-agent compaction: Sonnet/Opus and GPT-5.4-mini/GPT-5.5 child tools compact, while Haiku and GPT-5.3 Codex Spark/Sparks stay full.
- Direct WebFetch/WebSearch results and read-only/planning agent outputs (`explore`, `plan`, `decompose`, `reviewer`) stay full.

Key call: the tokenjuice **source repo is behind its own generated bundle** (bundle v0.8.0 carries generic-tool routing, model-aware gating and raw storage that aren't in \`src/\` yet), so regenerating from source would regress the bundle. All house policy therefore lives in a **wrapper in this repo** (\`extensions/tokenjuice/policy.mjs\`) around the pristine bundle — regeneration-proof, cache-safe (tool_result is post-hoc).

### The 4 diffs (one commit each)
1. **Policy layer** — per-class visible-char floors (bash 8k · ls/find 20k · grep/exec 32k), Agent results exempt initially, evidence-command patterns (test/CI/compiler/git-diff/logs) never compact, **raw-recovery guarantee** (a compaction without a readable raw file is dropped; raw files relocate from \`/tmp\` to \`~/.pi/agent/tokenjuice/\`). Config: L1 defaults ← \`extensionConfig.tokenjuice\` (L3) ← \`PI_TOKENJUICE_*\` env (L4). Peer range was already fixed in #140.
2. **Tests** — policy contract through the real composed entry (9 scenarios) + **cache-stability smoke**: host-surface proof the extension never touches \`registerTool\`/\`setActiveTools\`/system-prompt APIs, enabled or disabled. Wired into \`test:extension-gate:ci\`.
3. **Canary profile** — \`@valkyriweb/my-pi-full-tokenjuice-canary\` (static variant, boring load state). \`check-profiles\` gains a \`classifyAs\` alias; tokenjuice reclassified **canary-only**, so adding it to \`my-pi-full\` is now a validation error until the promotion criteria pass (documented in the extension README).
4. **Drift guard** — \`verify:tokenjuice-runtime\` fails when \`~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js\` diverges from the canonical bundle (oracle risk #7). Currently byte-identical.

### Gates
- \`test:tokenjuice:smoke\` (bundle contract + policy contract + cache smoke) ✅
- \`check:profiles\` ✅ · \`check:runtime-inventory\` ✅ · \`test:profiles:e2e\` 7/7 ✅ · \`verify:tokenjuice-runtime\` ✅

### Follow-up (not in this PR — needs Luke)
tokenjuice currently auto-loads into **every** Pi session via \`~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js\` (outside the profile system), which contradicts the verdict's hold-out. To match the verdict: rename it to \`tokenjuice.js.disabled\` and run canary sessions via the new profile.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/luke/.claude/skills/autoreview

# Auto Review

Run the bundled structured review helper as a closeout check. This is code review, not Guardian `auto_review` approval routing.

Codex review is the default when no engine is set. It usually delivers the best review results and should remain the normal final closeout engine.

Use when:

- user asks for Codex review / Claude review / autoreview / second-model review
- after non-trivial code edits, before final/commit/ship
- reviewing a local branch or PR branch after fixes

Keep going until structured review returns no accepted/actionable findings. If a review-triggered fix changes code, rerun focused tests and rerun the structured review helper.

Be patient with large bundles. Structured review can be silent for several minutes while the model call is active, especially with Codex tools or web search. Treat `review still running: ... elapsed=... pid=...` as healthy progress, not a hang. Do not kill a review just because it has been quiet for 2–5 minutes. Inspect the process only after multiple heartbeat intervals or an obviously failed subprocess; prefer letting the same helper command finish.

Full advisory/rejection/suppression/Gitcrawl rules: references/contract.md (read when applying findings, handling suppression, or hitting Gitcrawl errors).

## Pick Target

Dirty local work:

```bash
<autoreview-helper> --mode local
```

Use this only when the patch is actually unstaged/staged/untracked in the current checkout. For committed, pushed, or PR work, point the helper at the commit or branch diff instead; do not force `--mode local` / `--uncommitted` just because the helper docs mention dirty work first. A clean local review only proves there is no local patch.

Branch/PR work:

```bash
<autoreview-helper> --mode branch --base origin/main
```

Optional review context is first-class:

```bash
<autoreview-helper> --mode branch --base origin/main --prompt-file /tmp/review-notes.md --dataset /tmp/evidence.json
```

If an open PR exists, use its actual base:

```bash
base=$(gh pr view --json baseRefName --jq .baseRefName)
<autoreview-helper> --mode branch --base "origin/$base"
```

Committed single change:

```bash
<autoreview-helper> --mode commit --commit HEAD
```

or with the helper:

```bash
~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD
```

Use commit review for already-landed or already-pushed work on `main`. Reviewing clean `main` against `origin/main` is usually an empty diff after push. For a small stack, review each commit explicitly or review the branch before merging with `--base`.

## Parallel Closeout

Format first if formatting can change line locations. Then it is OK to run tests and review in parallel:

```bash
skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --parallel-tests "<focused test command>"
```

Tradeoff: tests may force code changes that stale the review. If tests or review lead to code edits, rerun the affected tests and rerun review until no accepted/actionable findings remain. Once that rerun exits cleanly, stop; do not spend another long review cycle on redundant confirmation.

## Context Efficiency

Run the helper directly so target selection, engine choice, structured validation, and exit status all stay in one path. If output is noisy, summarize the completed helper output after it returns; do not ask another agent or reviewer to rerun the review.

Engines and panels (Pi engines, `--reviewers`, per-engine `--model`/`--thinking`): references/engines-and-panels.md (read when using multi-reviewer panels or Pi engines).

Helper paths and flags: references/helper-reference.md (read when looking up paths, flags, or mode selection logic).

## Final Report

Include:

- review command used
- tests/proof run
- findings accepted/rejected, briefly why
- the clean review result from the final helper/review run, or why a remaining finding was consciously rejected

Do not run another review solely to improve the final report wording. If the final helper run exited 0 and produced no accepted/actionable findings, report that exact run as clean.

`renderProfileSnapshot` now skips the write when `existing === data` (line 134), so the snapshot file's mtime is no longer bumped when content is unchanged. But `ensureProfileSnapshot` (line 195) decides whether to re-render via `newestSource > snapMtime`.

If a consolidation touches a curated file without changing its bytes (e.g. autoDream re-serializes identical content, or a `touch`), the source mtime permanently exceeds the now-frozen snapshot mtime, so every subsequent session_start calls `renderProfileSnapshot` again — re-reading both curated files and re-rendering — instead of the documented 'No-op (byte-stable) when fresh' (lines 166-170; mirrored in index.ts:244). Previously the unconditional write bumped the snapshot mtime past the source, letting the staleness check settle after one render.

Impact is low: two small file reads plus a string compare per session, and the base stays byte-identical so the prompt cache is unaffected — but it is a behavioral regression of a documented property. Fix: bump the snapshot mtime on skip (e.g. `utimes`) or have `ensureProfileSnapshot` compare rendered content rather than rely on the write advancing mtime.

33	
34	`<anything> || true` is always `true`, so this `assert.ok` can never fail regardless of which events were registered. The loop over `registeredEvents` is dead — it asserts nothing.
35	
36	The suite's real invariant (registration/firing touch no FORBIDDEN_HOST_APIS) is covered by the assertions at lines 94-96 and 110-112, so this is test-hygiene, not a hole in the core guarantee. But a committed always-true assertion reads as coverage it doesn't provide. Either delete lines 99-104, or — if the intent was to assert lifecycle hooks are absent — drop the `|| true` so it actually checks `!['before_agent_start','session_start'].includes(event)` (note the inline comment says such hooks are *allowed*, which contradicts that reading — clarify intent first).

39	extensions/tokenjuice/policy.mjs:190
40	policy.mjs:188-194: `withPolicy` delegates via `const shim = Object.create(pi)` and overrides only `shim.on`. Other calls (`registerCommand`, `appendEntry`, …) resolve up the prototype chain and run with `this===shim`.
41	
42	Verified safe for the current host: loader.ts builds `ExtensionAPI` as an object literal whose every method closes over `extension`/`runtime`/`cwd`/`eventBus` and never reads `this`; and the generated bundle consumes `pi` purely by method call (pi.on/appendEntry/registerCommand at 9449-9469) — never destructuring, spreading, or `Object.keys(pi)`, which `Object.create` would hide on the prototype. So this is not a runtime bug today.
43	
44	It is a latent coupling: the shim breaks the moment any future host method relies on `this`, or any consumer own-enumerates the `pi` object. An explicit forwarding object (spread the methods you intend to proxy, or `Reflect`-bind) would make the dependency visible instead of relying on the whole API staying closure-based. Worth a comment at minimum given this is the load-bearing entry wrapper.

49

The OR'd `text.includes('tokenjuice compacted')` is a content heuristic: any tool whose visible output merely contains that literal — e.g. `cat`-ing this policy file or the docs, a grep over the repo, or a test log echoing the phrase — is treated as already-compacted and skipped, so genuinely large output silently bypasses compaction.

cache-stability.test.mjs:100-103: `assert.ok(!['before_agent_start','session_start'].includes(event) || true, 'informational: …')`.

`<anything> || true` is always `true`, so this `assert.ok` can never fail regardless of which events were registered. The loop over `registeredEvents` is dead — it asserts nothing.

The suite's real invariant (registration/firing touch no FORBIDDEN_HOST_APIS) is covered by the assertions at lines 94-96 and 110-112, so this is test-hygiene, not a hole in the core guarantee. [P3] withPolicy's Object.create(pi) shim silently couples correctness to the host API being `this`-free
extensions/tokenjuice/policy.mjs:190
policy.mjs:188-194: `withPolicy` delegates via `const shim = Object.create(pi)` and overrides only `shim.on`. Other calls (`registerCommand`, `appendEntry`, …) resolve up the prototype chain and run with `this===shim`.

Verified safe for the current host: loader.ts builds `ExtensionAPI` as an object literal whose every method closes over `extension`/`runtime`/`cwd`/`eventBus` and never reads `this`; and the generated bundle consumes `pi` purely by method call (pi.on/appendEntry/registerCommand at 9449-9469) — never destructuring, spreading, or `Object.keys(pi)`, which `Object.create` would hide on the prototype. So this is not a runtime bug today.

It is a latent coupling: the shim breaks the moment any future host method relies on `this`, or any consumer own-enumerates the `pi` object. An explicit forwarding object (spread the methods you intend to proxy, or `Reflect`-bind) would make the dependency visible instead of relying on the whole API staying closure-based. Worth a comment at minimum given this is the load-bearing entry wrapper.

policy.mjs:136: `if (event?.details?.tokenjuice?.compacted === true || text.includes('tokenjuice compacted')) return false;`.

The structured `details.tokenjuice.compacted === true` check is the reliable idempotency guard. The OR'd `text.includes('tokenjuice compacted')` is a content heuristic: any tool whose visible output merely contains that literal — e.g. `cat`-ing this policy file or the docs, a grep over the repo, or a test log echoing the phrase — is treated as already-compacted and skipped, so genuinely large output silently bypasses compaction.

Low blast radius (only suppresses an optimization; no data loss), but it's a control-flow decision driven by sniffing untrusted tool output. Non-hermetic tests. policy.test.mjs and cache-stability.test.mjs set `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` to a temp dir — clearly intending to sandbox the settings read — but the policy ignores it and reads the developer's real `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. The moment a `extensionConfig.tokenjuice` entry is added there (a documented, supported override, e.g. `enabled:false`, a custom `minVisibleChars`, or `requireRawRecovery:false`), assertions 1–8 can flip and the gate breaks on Luke's machine while CI (clean home) stays green.
22	2. Production divergence. Under a non-default `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, global `extensionConfig.tokenjuice` overrides are read from the wrong directory and silently ignored, while the bundle's own auto-compaction flag honors the right one. The `process.cwd()` project path likewise diverges from `ctx` for child agents / server-mode / any cwd that isn't the session project.
23	
24	Fix: mirror the bundle — `const agentDir = process.env.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR || join(homedir(), ".pi", "agent")` for the global file, and prefer the session project root over `process.cwd()`.

31	The change adds a conservative policy wrapper around the pristine generated tokenjuice bundle, a canary-only profile, a profile-classification gate, a runtime drift guard, and three smoke tests. `settingsConfig()` hardcodes the global path `join(homedir(), ".pi", "agent", "settings.json")` and resolves the project file from `process.cwd()`. The generated bundle resolves the same settings differently: `agentDir = process.env.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR || join(home, ".pi", "agent")` (tokenjuice.generated.js:8984) and the project root from `getProjectRoot(ctx)` (9406). Non-hermetic tests. policy.test.mjs and cache-stability.test.mjs set `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` to a temp dir — clearly intending to sandbox the settings read — but the policy ignores it and reads the developer's real `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. 2. Production divergence. Under a non-default `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, global `extensionConfig.tokenjuice` overrides are read from the wrong directory and silently ignored, while the bundle's own auto-compaction flag honors the right one. Either extend the exempt check to `bashOutput` and source the command from `event.details` for that class, or qualify the README to say the exemption covers foreground bash + exec/grep only.
